title: Elastic capacity choreography and failsafe - PRD draft
content:
Status: draft - working brain dump / early design notes.

TL;DR
We propose an "elastic capacity choreography" layer for Dedicated pools that treats short bursts, longer surges, and isolation as first-class primitives. The goal is predictable P95 latency for top-tier customers while maximizing utilizable reserved compute and reducing hard preemptions. Keywords in this doc: elastic threads, handshake lanes, isolation curtains, grace windows, weave fallback.

Problem statement
- Dedicated customers commit GPU capacity but workloads are spiky (chat sessions, generative inference spikes, overnight batch embeddings). Today we either: keep large warm pools (wasteful), or perform hard evictions which create noisy neighbor incidents and user-visible latency spikes.
- Existing approaches (static burst credits, naive autoscale) trade either cost or reliability. We need a composable control plane that: 1) lets customers keep high utilization, 2) guarantees tail latency for selected SLOs, and 3) provides clear operational semantics for fallbacks.

Goals
- Primary: keep P95 latency <= baseline target for SLO-protected routes under 95th percentile load scenarios.
- Secondary: increase effective utilization of reserved capacity by 10-25% vs today without increasing customer-visible errors.
- Tertiary: expose clear primitives to customers and SEs (elastic_threads, containment_mode, graceful-fallback-policy).

Non-goals
- This doc is not a spec for cluster-level preemption internals (that's infra's area). We only define control primitives and operator-facing runbooks and approximate resource accounting.

Concept overview
- Elastic threads: logical micro-slices within a tenant's reservation. Each thread has a soft concurrency and a softness horizon (e.g., 30s). Threads can be temporarily overcommitted across tenants if global utilization allows. Threads are fast to spin up (no cold-model load) because they reuse warmed model instances and KV caches.
- Handshake lanes: brief, policy-driven channels to borrow capacity from other dedicated pockets or opportunistic pools. Loans are governed by lease units and repayment (headroom credits). Lanes are prioritized by SLO weight.
- Isolation curtains: dynamic QoS fences that tighten resource isolation when a tenant approaches SLO risk. Curtains can be applied to single model routes, entire tenants, or pools. Curtains reduce allowed concurrency and enable traffic shaping rather than hard eviction.
- Grace windows: short degradation windows (e.g., 10s) where degraded responses (lower fidelity quantized variants or cached-prefix responses) are allowed automatically before falling back to external hosted models.

Control plane primitives (customer-facing and operator-facing)
- elastic_threads: min/target/max (example: min=1,target=4,max=16). Internals translate this into weighted slots on gpus.
- containment_mode: {none, soft, strict} — determines how aggressively isolation curtains are enforced and whether preemption is allowed.
- handshake_policy: {allowed_partner_pools, max_lease_secs, repayment_smoothing} — defines borrowing rules.
- fallback_policy: ordered list of fallbacks: [same-pool-quantized, handshake-borrow, partner-fallback, hosted-fallback].

SLOs and metrics
- Route-level SLOs: p50/p95/p99 latency; error-rate; bounded-fallback-frequency.
- Operational goals: keep fallback-rate < 1% for protected routes; keep graceful-degrade < 3% for standard routes.
- Key metrics to collect and show in Console: real-time thread utilization, curtain-level per-tenant, handshake usage (leases active), warm-cache hit-rate, fallback invocations by type, predicted headroom delta.

Failure modes and runbook snippets
1) Rapid surge exhausting threads -> system applies isolation curtain (soft) and reduces target concurrency. If P95 still violated after grace window, attempt handshake borrow from pre-approved partner pool. If handshake denied, escalate to hosted-fallback.
Runbook excerpt: check thread utilization dashboard -> identify active handshakes -> if handshake_count>0 and repayment backlog>threshold open incident priority P2 -> notify SE and throttle non-protected routes.
2) Handshake partners fully utilized -> fallback to quantized model variant automatically; increase warm-cache retention for quantized variants for 60s.
3) Repeated preemption for a tenant -> mark tenant with containment_mode=strict for 24 hours and schedule SE outreach + billing credit review.

API and Console UX notes (rough)
- New API fields on reservation update: "elastic_threads": {"min":1,"target":4,"max":16}, "containment_mode":"soft", "handshake_policy":"partner-pool-arn:...,max_lease_secs:120". (This is a proposal - infra will review shape.)
- Console: visual "choreography map" for pool presidents — shows threads allocated, active handshakes (with TTL bars), current curtains, and fallback budget. Quick buttons: "request emergency loan" (trial), "apply curtain" (operator).

Operational cost and billing implications
- Handshakes and borrowed compute should accrue to the borrowing tenant as a separate line item with a higher rate (to disincentivize overuse). There will also be a small monthly handshake credit for enterprise customers.
- Containment_mode=strict might reduce tenant billable throughput; ops should surface potential crediting rules in Console during incident.

Rollout plan (phased)
- Phase 0 (Q1): Pilot with 2 internal tenants + one friendly external beta. Expose read-only telemetry and simulated handshakes.
- Phase 1 (Q2): Enable elastic_threads and curtains but default containment_mode=none; only soft handshakes allowed and require manual approval.
- Phase 2 (Q3): Auto-handshakes and billing integration; expose full Console controls; open to wider customers.

Open questions / TODOs
- How do we precisely convert elastic_threads -> GPU slot allocation across model families with differing memory/latency profiles? (infra + serving-runtime action)
- What is the right cost model for handshake repayment? flat per-second? per-token based? needs finance input (JIRA-DEDICATED-3421).
- UX: how much control should customers get vs operator-only? propose two-tier: SE-managed + tenant-managed.

Next steps (near term)
- Synthesize requirements for infra: slot allocator changes, lease ledger prototype. Owner: Marco. Due: 2025-02-10.
- Small prototype: implement curtain enforcement in sandbox and measure P95 improvements on synthetic spikes. Owner: Priya. Due: 2025-02-21.
- Draft billing model options for finance review. Owner: Samir. Due: 2025-02-28.

Notes to self
- Keep naming metaphors (choreography/weave/curtain) for internal docs only - stick to more direct terms in public-facing docs.
- Need to reconcile with Dedicated's existing "burst credit" ledger (lots of overlap).

References
- CONFLUENCE-PRD-7812 (capacity experiments), JIRA-DEDICATED-3421 (billing model task), infra PR 2145 (slot allocator sketch).

End of draft.
